by_phase.label: Foundations you can see (in flight, planned to the step)

items.title: Surfaces respond to light
items.visible_outcome: Stone reads as stone, wood as wood, leather as leather. Objects sit on the ground instead of floating on it. Shadowed areas have detail in them instead of being black.
items.closes_when: Protocol A is re-run blind against the same plates and we stop losing 5 of 5. Not when the orphan count reaches zero — statistics can fail a build and can never pass one.
items.unevidenced_note: closes_when needs a REPEAT of Protocol A (a fresh blind-judgement verdict at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r2.json or later) that clears the pass threshold. That file does not exist yet, so this item cannot read as done no matter what evidence its sub-steps accumulate.

items.title: Bind the material set — the orphan fix
items.visible_outcome: The player's body and every affected surface (305 of 406 materials) actually run the surface shader whose uniforms they already carry, instead of the uniforms sitting unread in userData.
items.closes_when: The CONSUMPTION arms (before/after) are filed and a hardware before/after sweep, both arms on the same Pod and the same GPU, confirms the orphan count went 305 to 0 and the rendered pixels differ.
items.unevidenced_note: This is sub-step (a) only. Step-1's own closes_when (a fresh blind Protocol A re-run) is separate and NOT yet evidenced — see step-1's own entry.

items.title: Contact shadows and ambient occlusion
items.visible_outcome: Objects sit on the ground instead of floating on it — the defect judges named 5 of 5, the most universal finding in the blind round.
items.closes_when: A contact-shadow or AO term is present in the render path (not just declared in FEATURE_CONSUMERS) and a before/after capture shows darkening at contact points that was not there before.

items.title: Ambient/GI fill with tone-mapped shadow lift
items.visible_outcome: Shadowed areas have detail in them instead of being crushed to black.
items.closes_when: An ambient/GI fill term is present in the render path and a before/after capture shows detail recoverable in a previously-black shadow region.

items.title: The first five minutes look and behave right
items.visible_outcome: You come out of character creation in Thorn, facing somewhere sensible, in a town that looks like a Black Marsh tidewater settlement, and you can walk out of the door without being inside another building.
items.closes_when: A hardware capture of the real opening path, many angles plus motion, looks right to a person.
items.unevidenced_note: closes_when is a human-judgement condition ('looks right to a person') with no filed verdict yet — ROADMAP.md itself says the capture daemon returned zero frames under load, so 'nobody has looked at any of the Thorn work'. Evidence for DONE should be a blind-judgement or capture-review verdict naming this step; none exists on disk, so this cannot be marked done by any mechanical proxy.

items.title: Buildings are not inside each other
items.visible_outcome: Doors open into streets rather than into other buildings.
items.closes_when: The 76 interpenetrating pairs (25 with a door inside another building) are resolved. Resolver work is done: game/src/world/footprint.js is now the single implementation of the collision geometry (there were three private copies, two of which agreed with each other over a rectangle the world does not have, which is why the defect stayed invisible), and the check now correctly reports 76 where the old, wrong check reported 22. Shrinking alone clears only 6 of 76 — the interiors are native records with one centimetre of slack already spent — so the remaining 70 need repositioning at the generator, which is step 2c.
items.unevidenced_note: The visible outcome ('doors open into streets') is not yet true for all 76 remaining pairs — this item stays in_progress, not done, until step-2c closes.

items.title: Building layout: move the interpenetrating pairs at the generator
items.visible_outcome: The generator does not re-author the same building collisions on every regeneration; the remaining interpenetrating pairs (five Blackrose pairs authored exactly 1.0 m apart; thorn-gate/thorn-house-0 sharing an identical offset_m — not a coincidence) are repositioned at the source rather than hand-patched.
items.closes_when: The generator's placement logic no longer produces colliding offsets for these pairs, and node tools/check-building-overlap.mjs's frozen baseline can be re-frozen lower without any settlement's door-in-building count going up.
items.unevidenced_note: Not yet dispatched — ROADMAP.md places it below step 1 in priority ('step 1 is where the screen changes most'), so there is no builder assigned and nothing to evidence yet. This is the honest not_started case, not a gap in the tracker.

items.title: Conversation has depth, and looks like Morrowind
items.visible_outcome: Asking about one topic opens others, so a conversation branches outward instead of being a flat list; speakers disagree with each other; and the window looks like Morrowind's.
items.closes_when: Topic visibility and reachability rise substantially past their current measured floors (22% -> 50% and climbing across landed batches; ten topics reachable from no greeting; 100 of 865 npc.topics entries name nothing; 52-61% of NPCs advertise no subject of their own) and the dialogue window matches the vendored Morrowind screenshot REF-A12c.

items.title: The quests that exist are reachable
items.visible_outcome: The faction ladders go past rank 5, opening 21 already-authored quests that no player can currently reach.
items.closes_when: Twelve world_flags entries open the ladders past rank 5, and W1-18's quest delivery (563 records, all three audit numbers hitting their claimed values) stands independently critiqued as both restored and good.

items.title: Combat feel
items.visible_outcome: Fights that feel like Souls — readable animation, weight, a difficulty curve worth climbing, and a moment-to-moment feel worth repeating.
items.closes_when: Human judges actually fight the game (not view charts of enemy behaviour) and rate the animation, difficulty and feel — named explicitly by the owner as its own step, not a background property.
items.unevidenced_note: closes_when's human half — 'how good the combat is ... how fun it feels' — has no filed verdict and, per ROADMAP.md, no judge has yet been asked to fight anything rather than view a chart. No mechanical proxy is substituted here; a blind play-judgement verdict naming this step is the only evidence that should ever mark it done.
